subject: Proposal: 3-Week Accelerator Patch and Usage Smoothing for StarkMetrics POC
messages:
From: Arielle Cohen <arielle@starkmetrics.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@starkmetrics.com>
Date: Fri, 8 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Quick ask — 3-week patch and smoothing for the POC

Hi Ava,

Appreciate everything so far — the engineering team hit a surprising usage spike this week while load-testing one of our agents and we burned through roughly 35% more tokens than we expected. Given that we’re mid-eval and still validating the integration, procurement is asking if we can do a short runway adjustment rather than a full-term amendment.

High level ask: can Redwood provide a three-week accelerator patch (no change to list pricing) that includes:
- A small one-time extension of access to the current pilot environment (3 weeks)
- Up to 25% token smoothing on the next invoice for any overage during that period
- A single, clean amendment we can sign (procurement prefers consolidated paperwork)

I’ve attached our usage export so you can see the spike. Tom (cc) is on procurement and will handle the paperwork side. We’d like to move fast — is this something the team can approve?

Thanks,
Arielle Cohen
Head of AI Ops
StarkMetrics

Attachment: starkmetrics_usage_report.csv
From: Ava Chen <ava@redwood.com>
To: Arielle Cohen <arielle@starkmetrics.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@starkmetrics.com>, David Kim <david@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 9 Oct 2027 10:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — 3-week patch and smoothing for the POC

Hi Arielle —

Thanks for the heads up and for sending the usage file. Short answer: yes, we can support a narrow runway patch with smoothing, provided we lock in a quick set of guardrails so both sides are clear on scope and billing.

Proposed approach (minimal change):
1) 3-week accelerator patch starting when you confirm — extends the current pilot environment and keeps the same model variants and region.
2) Token smoothing: we can apply a one-time reconciliation credit equal to 25% of the spike over your baseline for that 3-week window (applied as a credit on the next invoice).
3) Engineering access: we’ll keep burst capacity enabled but limit it to the current pool to avoid capacity impacts for other pilots.
4) Paperwork: I’ll draft a 1-page amendment that references the existing PO/contract and captures the dates, credit mechanics, and signatories. We can route via DocuSign.

Before I push the amendment to Legal, quick clarifying Qs:
- Is the requested 3-week window starting next Monday (10/11) or immediately?
- Can you confirm the baseline you expect us to use to measure the spike (week of 9/20 or month of Sept)?

Looping David on capacity and priyom for billing mechanics so we can move quickly once you confirm.

— Ava
Ava Chen
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ava@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
From: David Kim <david@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava@redwood.com>, Arielle Cohen <arielle@starkmetrics.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Oct 2027 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — 3-week patch and smoothing for the POC

Ava / Arielle —

From an ops/capacity perspective we’re comfortable enabling a 3-week patch with the constraints Ava listed. We’ll pin the pilot to the current GPU pool and throttle at 80% sustained utilization to protect multi-tenant performance. If you expect consistent sustained increases beyond burst levels, we should chat about Dedicated capacity — but for a short runway this approach is safe.

Billing note (Priyom / Soojin please confirm): the smoothing credit can be recorded as a one-time invoice credit against the next bill tied to deal HB-8421. We’ll need a short statement of the baseline window to calculate the overage.

David
Director, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference

Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2027 09:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — 3-week patch and smoothing for the POC

Thanks — I ran the numbers against the CSV Arielle sent. If we set the baseline to the median week in September (wk of 9/13–9/19) the overage for the spike window is about 28,400 tokens. Applying a 25% smoothing credit yields a credit of ~7,100 tokens equivalent (we’ll convert to USD per the HB-8421 rate card).

Operational steps I need from StarkMetrics to finalize the amendment and the credit calculation:
- Confirm baseline window = week of 9/13–9/19 OR propose an alternate 30-day baseline.
- Confirm patch start date (AvA suggested 10/11).
- Procurement contact to confirm signer name and email for DocuSign.

I’ve attached a short amendment draft (redwood_poc_amendment_draft.pdf) that Ava can route to Legal; it includes the credit math and dates as editable fields. Once we have the baseline and start date I’ll finalize the credit and create the invoice hold.

— Priyom
Billing Lead, Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2027 18:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — 3-week patch and smoothing for the POC

Thanks all — confirming baseline = week of 9/13–9/19 and patch start = Monday 10/11. Procurement will sign; signer is Tom Nguyen (tom.nguyen@starkmetrics.com).

One small ask from procurement: can the amendment include a short clause that any smoothing credit applied is final and not eligible for refund/adjustment if usage drops retroactively? They want clean closeout language.

If that looks fine we’re good to get the DocuSign and the patch turned on Monday morning. Appreciate the fast turnaround.

— Arielle
Head of AI Ops, StarkMetrics
